folder_html:
LIVE PRECIPITATION

Precipitation intensity (NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity, dBZ, OBSERVED radar echo): LOWEST 5 Very Light cyan/blue (drizzle, mist) → Light greens (~20-30: light rain/snow) → Moderate dark green (~30-40: steady rain/snow) → Heavy yellow/orange (~40-50: heavy rain) → Severe red (~50-60: severe storms, hail possible) → Intense magenta/purple (~60-70: violent storms, large hail) → HIGHEST+ 70+ Extreme white (destructive hail, debris). Same dBZ always shows the same color in every season — rain, snow, lake-effect snow, thunderstorms. No echo (no precipitation) stays see-through so the map underneath shows.

How to read it in any season. Light greens are light rain in summer — and light snow in winter. Moderate dark green is steady rain or steady snow, including lake-effect bands. Heavy yellow/orange is heavy rain (or very heavy snow rates). Severe red means severe thunderstorms with hail possible; Intense magenta/purple means violent storms with large hail and flash flooding; Extreme white is reserved for the most destructive echoes. Radar sees precipitation particles, not air temperature, so one scale covers rain, snow, and thunderstorms all year. Where you see through the overlay, there is no precipitation right now.
